terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, transitive; passive mūtārī, to change, become different
evidence: Cic. Sen. 10: nec senectūs mōrēs mūtāverat
terms.comment: The general word. It also means to exchange one thing for another (see swap), and to change clothes.

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.31: quae commūtantur fīuntque contrāria (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Change wholly; most frequent in Cicero (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Or. 214: verbōrum ōrdinem immūtā (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: erat enim in illō virō cōmitāte condīta gravitās, nec senectūs mōrēs mūtāverat
phrases.english: for in that man gravity was seasoned with kindness, and old age had not changed his ways

phrases.latin: quid rīdēs? mūtātō nōmine dē tē fābula narrātur
phrases.english: why are you laughing? Change the name, and the story is about you

phrases.latin: Nōn satis est dolēre, nisi mōrēs mūtāre velīs.
phrases.english: Being sorry is not enough, unless you mean to change your ways.

sources: Lewis & Short: muto · Lewis & Short: commuto · Lewis & Short: immuto
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cicero-philosophica, loci-horatius, loci-corderius), checked against the editions named there.
